questions.question: Explain how coal was formed, step by step.
questions.expected_answer: About 250 to 300 million years ago, plants grew in swamp forests. When they died, they fell into the swamp water, which had little oxygen, so they did not rot away completely and piled up as peat. Rivers covered the peat with mud and sand, and more layers piled up. Over millions of years, the weight and heat squeezed the peat into coal, found in seams between layers of rock.

questions.question: Why is coal called a non-renewable resource?
questions.expected_answer: Coal took millions of years to form from ancient plants, under special conditions that no longer exist in the same way. Once it is mined and burnt, it is gone forever and cannot be replaced in a human lifetime, so the amount of coal is limited and will run out one day.

questions.question: Describe the uses of coal and the problems caused by burning it.
questions.expected_answer: Coal is used mainly in power stations to heat water into steam that spins turbines to make electricity. It is also used to make coke for steel, liquid fuel and chemicals, for heating and cooking, and for export. Burning it releases smoke, dust and gases that harm health, cause acid rain, and release carbon dioxide that adds to climate change.
